text:
incident-bot: PAGER — Severity: SEV2. KV cache fragmentation spike in runtime pool eu-west-1. Observed sudden GPU memory climb (~70% of nodes >85% GPU mem), continuous-batching queue length up 4x, increased 5xxs for generation endpoints. Auto-escalation: paging on-call.
sara: Acked. I'm oncall for eng-sre. Looking now. Any customer-visible errors? ashley, can you confirm support tickets? :eyes:
ashley: We've got 3 inbound chats from EU customers about intermittent errors and timeouts. One customer reported long tail latency ~6-8s on streaming. No confirmed data exfil/issues. Raising to severity.
leo: jumping in — runtime team. Initial graphs show fragmentation on KV arena allocators, lots of small free slabs and failed cudaMalloc fallbacks. Stacktraces show repeated arena reslice and fallback to device malloc. Suspect recent compaction change + longer TTL for cached kv entries.
maya: from ML infra: continuous batching saw a policy change earlier today (max_batch_size bumped from 64 -> 128 and batch_ttl increased). That increases simultaneous KV working set per request. Could be causing more frequent KV growth and fragmentation.
leo: running a quick check: `kubectl exec -it runtime-pool-eu-0 -- curl -s localhost:9090/metrics | grep kv_arena_frag` -> frag_ratio ~0.62 on affected pods vs 0.12 baseline. OOMs seen in dmesg from CUDA with `CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY` followed by fallbacks. Copying log snippet:

```
[2024-11-12T09:12:03Z] runtime: kv_arena_reslice: requested 512KB, available 64KB -> fragmentation
[2024-11-12T09:12:04Z] cuda: malloc failed on device 0: CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY
[2024-11-12T09:12:04Z] runtime: fallback to host-pinned fallback allocator
```

leo: Hot mitigation idea: roll back batch size change or apply temporary per-pool batch throttle, and trigger arena compaction across affected nodes. Compaction can be noisy — prefer staged.
sara: Agreed. Two parallel actions: 1) quick throttle to stop further pressure (low-risk) 2) targeted compaction/defrag on quiet nodes. If compaction causes increased latencies, we revert throttle.
tom: I'm on infra side. I can push a routing throttle via the smart-router to limit max_concurrent_batches on eu-west-1 from 600 -> 250. That should reduce concurrency quickly without requiring node restarts. Preparing change now.
ops-bot: Change queued: set routing.max_concurrent_batches[eu-west-1]=250 by tom at 2405123560. Will apply in 10s.
ops-bot: Change applied: routing.max_concurrent_batches[eu-west-1]=250. Observing.
maya: After throttle, batch queue length dropped ~60% within 45s. Good signal. Error rate on generation endpoints dropped from 6.8% -> 1.9%. GPU mem usage still high on some stale pods.
leo: Initiating controlled compaction run on five least-loaded pods (runtime-pool-eu-0-2..6). Command I'm running:

```
kubectl exec runtime-pool-eu-0-2 -- /usr/local/bin/kv-arena-compact --vacuum --quiet
```

leo: Running compaction in series with 30s wait between pods to avoid simultaneous spikes.
sara: Noted. Ashley, can you send a short customer-facing update to impacted folks? Keep messaging to: "We're mitigating elevated latency in EU region; temporary throttles applied; no data loss." Keep it minimal.
ashley: Sent update to active chats and created incident banner for EU customers. Link: https://support.redwood.ai/cases/INC-2042
leo: Compaction progress: pod -2: success, freed ~1.2GB of device-side fragmentation. pod -3: success, freed ~900MB. pod -4: compaction started -> small pause in serving as expected. Observed one spike in tail latency to 9s during compaction on that pod.
maya: Monitoring model throughput — throughput dip temporary but overall tail latency trending down. Good.
leo: After compaction on targeted pods, frag_ratio for those dropped to ~0.15. However, 2 pods still show high frag ~0.55 likely because they had large long-lived KV prefixes (customer A pinned models). Propose: 1) add TTL eviction for caches with >X prefixes, 2) revert batch_ttl/max_batch_size to previous values as a safety rollback.
sara: Approve rollback of the batch policy. leo or maya, what's the quick config change? Is it runtime config (hot) or requires rollout?
maya: It's a global policy in config service, can be hot-changed. Rolling to set max_batch_size back to 64 and batch_ttl to 120ms. I'll patch now.
maya: Patch applied: batch_policy.max_batch_size=64, batch_policy.batch_ttl_ms=120. Verified via `curl config-service/internal/policies/batch`.
ops-bot: Config change detected at 2405123800 by maya: batch_policy updated.
maya: Immediately after change, average concurrency dropped and we saw GPU mem pressure easing across the pool. Error rates down to 0.6% and latency back to normal band.
leo: For the two stubborn pods, I'm scheduling lifecycle restart to fully reclaim arena memory. Plan: drain -> restart container -> undrain.
sara: Go ahead. Coordinate with tom for node drains if needed.
tom: Drains scheduled. Restarting pod runtime-pool-eu-0-9 now.
ops-bot: runtime-pool-eu-0-9 restarted at 2405123955. Health checks green.
leo: After restarts, frag ratios cleared across the pool. GPU mem usage normalized to baseline. Continuous batch queue stable. No more cuda malloc fallbacks.
ashley: Customers notified: follow-up message sent saying mitigation complete and we're investigating root cause. One customer reply thanked us for fast action.
sara: Great work. Post-incident next steps (to be tracked in postmortem):
- owner: leo
- timeline capture and exact config diff (maya)
- add new alert: kv_arena_frag > 0.4 for >5m AND cuda_malloc_fallbacks > 10 -> SEV2 pager (sara)
- evaluate automatic background compaction or preemptive eviction policy (runtime team)
- revert/cleanup temporary routing throttle after 1h if stable (tom)
leo: I'll own the postmortem and propose a safer default for batch_policy changes (auto-smoke for fragmentation impact) and an automatic canary for large max_batch_size changes.
sara: I'll close the pager once we confirm 30m of stability. Leaving the channel open for any follow-ups.
incident-bot: Incident: RESOLVED by sara at 2405124120 — impact: reduced tail latency & error rate for eu-west-1. Follow-up: postmortem assigned to leo.
